# 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's reign, Abijah became king of Judah.

**2** He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother was Micaiah daughter of Uriel, from Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

**3** Abijah went into battle with an army of 400,000 able fighting men, while Jeroboam lined up against him with 800,000.

**4** Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and shouted: "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!

**5** Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom of Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?

**6** Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat — a mere servant of Solomon son of David — rebelled against his master.

**7** A gang of worthless troublemakers rallied around him and overpowered Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young and indecisive, unable to resist them.

**8** "And now you think you can resist the LORD's kingdom, which is in the hands of David's descendants, just because you have a huge army and those golden calves Jeroboam made for you as gods?

**9** Haven't you driven out the LORD's priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? Haven't you appointed your own priests the way pagan nations do? Anyone who shows up with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of your so-called gods — which are not gods at all.

**10** But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned Him. The priests who serve the LORD are descendants of Aaron, and the Levites assist them.

**11** Every morning and evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the bread on the ceremonially clean table and light the gold lampstand every evening. We are fulfilling our obligations to the LORD our God. But you have abandoned Him.

**12** God Himself is with us — He is our leader. His priests are here with their trumpets, ready to sound the battle cry against you. Men of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors. You will not win!"

**13** Meanwhile, Jeroboam had secretly sent troops to circle behind them. So his main force faced Judah from the front while the ambush waited behind them.

**14** When Judah turned and saw they were being attacked from both front and rear, they cried out to the LORD. The priests blew their trumpets,

**15** and the men of Judah raised the battle cry. As they shouted, God routed Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

**16** The Israelites fled before Judah, and God handed them over.

**17** Abijah and his troops inflicted heavy casualties — 500,000 of Israel's best soldiers fell that day.

**18** The Israelites were subdued on that occasion, and the people of Judah were victorious because they relied on the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

**19** Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured several of his towns: Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their surrounding villages.

**20** Jeroboam never regained his power during Abijah's lifetime. The LORD struck him down, and he died.

**21** But Abijah grew powerful. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

**22** Everything else about Abijah — his conduct and his sayings — is recorded in the annotations of the prophet Iddo.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **13:5**: "Covenant of salt" — in the ancient world, salt meant permanence. Abijah is saying: God's commitment to David's line cannot expire. You're fighting an everlasting covenant.

- **13:12**: Abijah's sermon before battle is one of the longest pre-battle speeches in the Bible. His argument is simple: we have the real God, the real priests, and the real worship. You have golden calves. Choose wisely.

- **13:18**: "Because they relied on the LORD" — the Chronicler's bottom line. Not because they were braver, better trained, or more numerous (they were outnumbered 2:1). Because they trusted God. That's the Chronicler's theory of everything.


— PNEUMA
